name: Telegraph cryptic crossword, All New book 4 No 9

book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Unwise to relinquish right, showing a lack of respect

indicators.note: to relinquish something is to give it up, so a letter is dropped from the first word

blocks.note: unwise means lacking prudence
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly giving up a right comes across as disrespectful.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the R out of IMPRUDENT to leave IMPUDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent means cheeky or insolent, behaviour that shows no respect for others.

clue.text: Soldiers attempt to follow home supporter

indicators.note: one piece following the others means it is placed after them

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
a fan supports a team
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Troops try to track down a supporter of the home side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' looks like the home team, but being in means being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The infantry are foot soldiers, the part of an army that fights on foot.

clue.text: "Put a coat on quietly" isn't commonly said!

blocks.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Someone objects that 'put a coat on quietly' is not an everyday phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits inside the quotation marks, though it reads as part of a quoted remark.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint something is to apply a coat of colour to it.

clue.text: Fighting fund, etc, is now no longer in force

indicators.note: things fighting are thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A war chest and similar resources have lapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighting fund' looks like one phrase, but 'Fighting' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct has ceased to exist or operate, such as a law no longer valid.

clue.text: Lacking the go-ahead in this secluded place?

blocks.note: lacking means having no
an OK is permission to proceed

explanation.surface: A hidden corner where nobody has been given permission.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a sheltered corner or out-of-the-way spot.

clue.text: Fires across the top of motor boats

indicators.note: one thing set across another lies over it on both sides, so the first word wraps round the letter
'the top of' keeps only the first letter of 'motor'

blocks.note: to fire staff is to sack them
the top, or first letter, of motor

explanation.surface: Flames spread over the upper parts of some motor boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Put M inside SACKS. A smack is a small sailing fishing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a traditional single-masted fishing vessel, so smacks are a kind of boat.

clue.text: Rum load distributed in individual units

indicators.note: what is distributed is spread around, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A shipment of rum is shared out in single portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink, but here it is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Modular describes something built from separate standard components or modules.

clue.text: Sort of car accountant with spirit allowed

blocks.note: CA is a chartered accountant
brio is liveliness or spirit
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An accountant drives a type of car with lively permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests a drink, but here it means vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriolet is a car with a folding roof, a convertible.

clue.text: A big step for setter oddly accepting free…
Goes mad about failure of footwear!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the second

blocks.note: to flip is to lose one's temper or go crazy
a flop is a failure

explanation.surface: Someone flies into a rage when their shoes fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failure of footwear' reads as a single phrase, but 'failure' belongs to the wordplay and 'footwear' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip-flops are light rubber sandals held on by a thong between the toes.

clue.text: … agents at loggerheads do absolutely nothing
Exclude expensive cover for bishop

indicators.note: a cover goes all round what it protects, so one word encloses the letter

blocks.note: dear means costly
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A costly hat or cloak for a bishop is ruled out.
explanation.walkthrough: DEAR wraps round B.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar is to bar or shut out someone from a place or right.

clue.text: Observing cannot, in general, hide it

indicators.note: the words of the phrase conceal the answer within their run of letters

blocks.note: found across the joins of these words

explanation.surface: Someone watching generally cannot conceal what they see.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside caNNOT IN General.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting something means observing or taking notice of it.

clue.text: Man with a canary in a cage?

definitions.text: Man with a canary in a cage?

blocks.note: a cage is slang for a prison
a canary is a bird, and also slang for an informer who sings

explanation.surface: A man keeps a pet canary in a birdcage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: the caged bird is the man himself, behind bars. The cage comes first in the answer, then the bird it holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A jailbird is a prisoner, often a habitual one, likened to a bird kept in a cage.

clue.text: Gets a cold before church singers are heard

indicators.note: what is heard is only listened to, so the sound is kept and the spelling changes

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold
choirs, said out loud, matches quires, sets of paper sheets

explanation.surface: Someone catches a cold just before the church choir sings.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is 24 or 25 sheets of paper, and is pronounced like choir.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to get or obtain it.

clue.text: Surfer's aid for channel crossings?

blocks.note: surface reading: equipment for a surfer crossing the English Channel
setter's reading: the surfer is a channel-hopping TV viewer, and the crossings are switches from one channel to the next

explanation.surface: Something to help a surfer get across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel surfing is flicking between TV channels, which you do from your seat with a handset.
explanation.definitionFit: The handset that changes television channels from a distance is the device a channel surfer relies on.

clue.text: Mark and the rest operate this craft!

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for the mark, a former German currency
et al is Latin shorthand for and others
to work a machine is to operate it

explanation.surface: Mark and the others crew a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a vessel to operate, but it means a skilled trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalwork is the craft of shaping metal into objects.

clue.text: Cheer up — prison changes the name!
Convoluted language employed by a conman?

definitions.text: Convoluted language employed by a conman?

blocks.note: a tongue is a language, as in mother tongue
a twister is a swindler or cheat

explanation.surface: A swindler bamboozles his victims with tangled talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, and inside it the language of a twister, a cheat, builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue twister is a phrase such as 'she sells sea shells' that is convoluted and hard to say quickly.

clue.text: Figure that might lure man astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so these letters are scattered

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: An alluring figure might lead a man off the straight and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests someone's body, but here it is a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A numeral is a figure or symbol standing for a number.

clue.text: Stamp for letters typed in support of one motorway
21_ 'Rip-off sort of tool

blocks.note: first meaning: to cheat, a sense of the verb in slang
second meaning: a bladed tool for cutting wood or stone

explanation.walkthrough: The verb meaning to swindle and the woodworker's tool are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chisel is informal for swindling someone, and a chisel is a woodworking blade.

clue.text: Distinguishing feature of hotel brand welcoming everybody

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so one part holds the other

blocks.note: H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet
all means everybody
a brand is a trade mark

explanation.surface: A hotel chain's signature touch is that it welcomes everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The hotel brand takes in everybody: hotel and brand stand outside, everybody sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hallmark is a characteristic sign, originally the stamp on assayed silver.

clue.text: Jumped, seeing head of state crash

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of state
prang is British slang for a minor crash, especially in a car

explanation.surface: A president leapt in alarm at news of a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British informal for a crash or to crash a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprang is the past tense of spring, to leap suddenly.

clue.text: Stadium in region outside the North

indicators.note: one word sitting outside the other surrounds it

blocks.note: an area is a region
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A sports ground is located in a northern district.
explanation.walkthrough: AREA goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed stadium for sport or spectacle.

clue.text: 25___ Eager to promote new joint

indicators.note: to promote is to move up, so one letter shifts higher in the word

blocks.note: keen means eager
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Keen to advance a fresh joint venture.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, promoting the N of KEEN moves it up, giving KNEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint between the thigh and the lower leg.

clue.text: Clean, cold, bitter outside

indicators.note: one word placed outside another sits around it

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
sour means bitter-tasting

explanation.surface: Clean, cold and bitter on the outside, like a description of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUR goes around C.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to clean by hard scrubbing.

clue.text: Feeling tense after having dispatched one crew

indicators.note: one part following another means the pieces are joined in that order

blocks.note: to dispatch is to send
I is the Roman numeral one
a crew is a body of men
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone feels nervous after sending a crew away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the feeling, but it is the grammar term, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a feeling or emotion, or an opinion coloured by one.

clue.text: Having a good chance of being similar to library that's empty

definitions.text: Having a good chance of being

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost everything inside, leaving only its outermost letters

blocks.note: like means similar to
the first and last letters of library

explanation.surface: A deserted library is apt to resemble another.
explanation.definitionFit: Likely describes something probable, with a good chance of happening or being so.

clue.text: Engineers make a strong effort to check

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to strain is to exert oneself hard

explanation.surface: Engineers work hard to keep something under control.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To check someone is to hold them back, which is what restrain means.
